Very useful. Key observations:

1. **The `{branch}`-dispatch rules that the dead-head scenario hits**: `review-on-label` (limit 1, ref {branch}, notLabels: []), `rework-on-label` (limit 1, ref {branch}, notLabels: []), `review-on-issue-label`, `review-after-dev`, etc. NONE of them exclude `validation_failed`. So once a dead head is parked `validation_failed` by gh-922, `review-on-label`/`rework-on-label` still match it (if they carry agent:review/agent:rework) and keep attempting every tick, consuming fallthrough reserve each tick. With the reserve fixed at 3, FOUR simultaneously dead `{branch}` heads under one limit:1 rule re-starve the FIFO (4 candidates dead → slice(0,4) exhausted, no slot). Also interesting: `rework-on-validation-failed` (labels: ['validation_failed']) — a gh-922-parked PR MATCHES this rule! What does that rule do? It arms agent:rework on validation_failed PRs? Let me check: "rework-on-validation-failed limit=1 labels=['validation_failed'] notLabels=['agent:rework','ai_validating']" — this rule (per gh-757/gh-917 family) arms agent:rework on parked PRs... for MACHINE PRs (per the rework-on-red-gate description, guests keep the human-push semantics; machine PRs get a rework arm). If the gh-922 dead-head park stamps validation_failed on a MACHINE PR (ai-teammate's own PR with a deleted branch — rare but possible), rework-on-validation-failed would arm agent:rework → rework-on-label dispatches a rework leg on `{branch}` → dispatch fails no-ref again → MORE marker comments (from a second rule) → the count climbs faster; the park guard (`already parked`) prevents re-park, but each failed dispatch of rework-on-label ALSO writes markers... wait no — recordDispatchFailure returns early because labels contain validation_failed (item.labels fetched fresh from the query — the PR now carries validation_failed). So no marker spam. But an arm_rework localAction stamping agent:rework on a dead-head-parked machine PR is a wasted arm; rework-on-label will attempt + fail + yield every tick. Self-limiting, minor.

But the deeper interaction: does arm_rework's in-flight latch etc. care? Fine.

2. **`park-reset` rule** (labels: ['validation_failed'], limit 10) — the RESET ladder: probes human push newer than park → clears the label. The gh-922 park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` which keys the parkedSince/sha-change probes. Good — the gh-922 park integrates with the existing reset ladder. Note: `park-reset`'s probes were built for RED parks (checks semantics). For a dead-head park, the "human push newer" probe needs the branch to EXIST again — parkResetCommit walks the head chain of the CURRENT head... if the branch doesn't exist, uHead=null → fail closed → park stays. When the author restores/re-pushes the branch, the head exists again, and the actor check ("human push NEWER than the validation_failed event") — parkedSince reads the label-add timestamp (the park event) — the re-push is newer → clears. Correct integration.

3. **The tier void only matters for `priority_blocker` carriers.** OK.

4. **`review-on-label` notLabels is EMPTY** — so a parked PR keeps matching review-on-label forever until the park resets. Each tick: 1 failed dispatch + 1 early-return recordDispatchFailure (no comment spam — the parked guard works). The wasted-attempt-per-tick is by design ("re-matches until the ref is restored").

Now the >3-dead-heads starvation: to hit it you need 4+ dead-head candidates AHEAD of an alive candidate in one rule's tier-sorted list with limit such that limit+reserve < dead count. E.g. review-on-label limit:1 with 4 abandoned `agent:review` PRs. Possible but requires 4 abandoned labeled PRs. IMPORTANT vs SUGGESTION? The ticket's core complaint is starvation; the fix bounds it at 3 concurrent dead heads. I'll file IMPORTANT with concrete options (scale reserve with limit; or exclude validation_failed+dead-head from dispatch-rule queries via notLabels — accepting the semantic conflation; or bump reserve). Actually — hmm, let me reconsider. The engine loop breaks on `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit`, iterating up to len(tickets) = limit+3. If all limit+3 candidates fail, the tick ends with 0 processed. Next tick, same. So starvation persists beyond 3 dead heads. BUT the parked dead heads accumulate markers only up to the cap; after parking they're SILENT (no more comments). A 4th dead head would park too (3 ticks). So steady state: unlimited dead heads, all parked, all attempted every tick, all failing — starvation if dead count >= limit+reserve... wait no! Each dead head attempt = 1 API call that fails fast. The loop iterates ALL tickets (not just limit+3 — well, exactly limit+3 tickets). With 4+ dead heads and limit 1, the slice is 4 — all dead → alive candidates beyond position 4 never reached. Starved. Yes, the bound is real. IMPORTANT.

Hmm — although... realistically, do dead-head PRs accumulate? PR-as-carrier rules consume labels on dispatch (consumeLabels) — review-on-label: does it consume agent:review on dispatch? If consumeLabels removes agent:review when the leg dispatches successfully, a PR whose dispatch ALWAYS fails keeps agent:review (never consumed) and keeps matching forever. Yes — that's exactly the ticket scenario (pr-1615 kept priority_blocker and matched every tick).

So: 4+ abandoned PRs carrying agent:review (or agent:rework) with deleted branches = starvation returns. Plausible on busy repos over months. IMPORTANT.

5. **Another design check — `triggerFailMarks` reads ALL comments of the PR every failed tick** — one `github_get_pr_comments` call per failed dispatch per tick. Cheap enough.

6. **Now the item.labels check in recordDispatchFailure uses `item.labels`** — for the github PR source, item.labels = label names array. ✓ (tests pass with labels arrays).

7. **`String(expandedRef || '') !== String(item.branch)`**: for `review-on-issue-label` (ref '{branch}' but item issue-carrier with linked PR branch) — item.branch set? The issue path sets item.branch only when a linked OPEN PR exists. OK.

8. **DRY mode**: recordDispatchFailure returns early in DRY — no side effects in dry ticks. ✓ And the DRY dispatch in triggerWorkflow returns `undefined` (not true/false) — unchanged behavior.

9. **GraalJS compliance of new code**: `var` + plain functions everywhere; no arrow functions, no let/const, no template literals. `String.prototype.replace` with regex, `Object.assign`? Not used in new code except tests (tests run in GraalJS too — `Object.assign` used in tests: `Object.assign({ realSource: true }, ...)` — is Object.assign available in GraalJS? ES6 builtins — GraalJS supports ES2020+, yes. And existing tests already use Object.assign (I saw `Object.assign({}, RULE, ...)` in existing test code). Fine.

10. **triggerFailures.js requires nothing** — no require at all. Pack-require rule satisfied trivially. smAgent.js requires it hoisted at top (line ~150). ✓ gh-823 rule respected.

11. **`classifyTriggerError` false-positive surface**: `/\b422\b/.test(s) && /ref/i.test(s)` — a transient error message containing "422" and "ref" anywhere (e.g. "422: Unprocessable Entity — invalid input ... refresh_token") would classify no-ref → marker+park path on a non-dead head. The second test even asserts `'422: Unprocessable Entity — invalid input'` → transient (no "ref" substring — wait, "invalid input" — does it contain "ref"? No. OK). Edge: a 422 about branch protection mentioning "required status checks... refs" — unlikely from a dispatch error. The classifier only drives COMMENT bookkeeping (worst case: spurious marker comments + park on a live head — that WOULD be bad: parking a live PR because its error text mentioned 422+ref... but the dispatch FAILED, so the PR isn't going anywhere this tick anyway; 3 such failures in a row = park. Eh — a persistently failing live head (e.g., workflow file 404 is classified transient ✓). Acceptable heuristic. Not a finding beyond maybe noting the message-shape coupling.

12. **The workflow budget**: failed candidates don't decrement `workflowBudget.remaining` ✓ (line 3735-3737: only on success). But `ensureWorkflowBudgetActiveCount` inside triggerWorkflow may still run…

{"content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: the fixed 3-slot reserve bounds the starvation fix — 4+ dead heads re-starve the FIFO**

`TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE = 3` is a hard constant, and a parked (`validation_failed`) dead head **remains a dispatch candidate** — the dispatch rules that hit this failure mode (`review-on-label`, `rework-on-label`, `review-after-dev`, …) carry `notLabels: []`, so a parked PR keeps matching every tick and burns one failed dispatch (plus one reserve slot) per tick until the branch is restored.

Failure shape after this fix, for a `limit: 1` rule with **4+** simultaneously dead heads:

```text
candidates (tier-sorted, slice(0, limit + 3)) = [dead1, dead2, dead3, dead4]
→ dead1 fails (yield), dead2 fails (yield), dead3 fails (yield), dead4 fails (yield)
→ loop ends: 0 slot credits, the alive candidate at position 5 was never in the slice
→ FIFO starved again, every tick
```

Each dead head parks after 3 ticks and goes silent, but parked heads are never removed from candidacy, so abandoned `agent:review`/`agent:rework` PRs accumulate indefinitely on a busy repo — the bound is real, not theoretical.

Options, cheapest first:

1. Scale the reserve: `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE + parkedCount` or a simple `Math.max(3, …)` heuristic.
2. Bench dead-head-parked candidates at source level: `validation_failed` + head missing from the already-fetched `branchHeads` snapshot identifies a dead-head park without any comment scan (do **not** exclude all `validation_failed` — the `park-reset` rule must still find red-parked PRs).
3. Add `notLabels: ["validation_failed"]` to the `{branch}`-dispatch rules in `sm_github.json` — accepted cost: it conflates the red-park (gh-832) and dead-head-park semantics on the shared label.

At minimum, document the 3-dead-head bound next to the constant so the next starvation ticket doesn't start from zero.

Related dead end worth noting: a **machine-authored** PR with a deleted head gets parked, `rework-on-validation-failed` arms `agent:rework` on it, but the rework leg can never dispatch (dead branch) and no human push will ever clear the park — a permanent arm + a permanent failed attempt per tick. Interesting and important: `sm_github.json` rules live in THIS repo and use `notLabels` exclusions extensively. Notably, the gh-832 convergence park description says "The parked PR leaves validate-armed's FIFO (notLabels excludes it)". So the validate-armed rule excludes validation_failed. But the AI-leg dispatch rules (review-on-label, rework-on-label, dev legs) — do THEY exclude validation_failed? The review-on-label rule dispatches ai-teammate.yml on `{branch}` — a parked dead head STILL matches review-on-label (no notLabels for validation_failed there, per the test which shows a parked PR still being attempted). So the review lane keeps attempting the parked head every tick — consuming reserve slots. That confirms my analysis: parked dead heads persist as candidates for dispatch rules that don't exclude validation_failed.

Key severity call: the ticket's ask #1-3 are implemented. The residual (reserve=3 bound; >3 dead heads re-starve; parked heads still consume one failed dispatch per tick per rule) is a design limitation worth IMPORTANT — with the concrete fix being `notLabels: ["validation_failed"]` on the dispatch rules (review-on-label / rework-on-label / dev legs) in sm_github.json, which the repo's own gh-832 precedent uses for validate-armed. Wait — but careful: review-on-label excluding validation_failed would mean a PR that's parked for validation can't get a review leg? Hmm — validation_failed means "validation CI is red-parked" in the gh-832 semantics — the REVIEW leg (ai:review) is a different lane and may legitimately want to run on a validation-parked PR (review is useful regardless of CI red). EXCLUDING validation_failed from review-on-label would change that semantics — parked-for-red PRs would never get review legs. That's a behavior change beyond this ticket. Hmm.

But for the DEAD-HEAD park specifically — the new gh-922 park reuses the SAME label `validation_failed`. So the label now carries two park semantics (red-park and dead-head-park) and any rule-level exclusion conflates them. The dead-head park comment text says "no legs are dispatched against it" — but the review lane will still attempt it. There's a genuine semantic-overload question here: reusing validation_failed for the dead-head park means the dead-head-parked PR is indistinguishable from a red-parked PR. An alternative would be a distinct label (e.g. `head_parked` / `dispatch_dead`) + tier void + exclusion from dispatch rules. The PR deliberately reuses validation_failed to inherit the #633 RESET probes ("parked-head: <sha> keys the existing #633 sticky-park RESET probes") — that's the rationale: reuse the reset ladder instead of building a new one. Defensible. The cost: rule-level disambiguation is impossible (can't exclude dead-head-parked without also excluding red-parked). This is worth an IMPORTANT or strong SUGGESTION about label semantics overloading + the reserve bound. Given the ticket explicitly asked for exactly this design ("park the PR with validation_failed + a comment... consistent with the existing sticky-park rule"), the reuse is owner-directed. So the label choice is per-ticket; NOT a finding against the PR. The residual starvation bound (>3 dead heads) though is a real limitation the ticket didn't specify — SUGGESTION level, since 3+ simultaneously-dead heads is rare and the ticket asked for a bounded heuristic. Hmm, "When in doubt, start one level higher". The starvation scenario was THE ticket. A fix that re-starves at >3 dead heads partially addresses it. But realistically: each dead head parks after 3 ticks and stays parked; 4+ abandoned-branch PRs one repo simultaneously in the same rule's query — plausible on a busy monorepo with churn. But each tick, the parked ones yield quickly (their dispatch fails fast ~1 API call each), and the alive candidate at position 4 still gets the slot if only 3 dead heads precede it. With 4+ dead heads: dead1..dead4 all fail, alive at position 5 — but slice(0, 1+3) = 4 candidates only → alive never reached → starvation. So the bound is real. I'll make this an IMPORTANT finding: recommend (a) excluding the dead-head-parked items from the candidate list — but can't distinguish labels... hmm, actually CAN they? The dead-head park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` — but source-level comment scanning would be expensive. OR (b) make TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE larger / scale with limit, or (c) have the engine skip candidates whose labels include validation_failed AND whose previous dispatch failed no-ref... Simplest robust: engine-side skip of already-parked candidates for rules that dispatch on {branch}... but again the red-park conflation. Alternatively the marker-park could use the `parked-head` sha: queryPrs already has access to branchHeads — a parked PR whose head no longer exists in branchHeads IS dead-head-parked (identifiable at source level WITHOUT comment scanning: label=validation_failed + head not in open branch heads!). Actually that's elegant: the source already fetches branch heads. But implementing head-existence checks per candidate adds complexity/cost. OK — my finding: IMPORTANT, with options. Actually, let me reconsider severity: is >3-dead-heads a "real maintainability or correctness issue"? It's a correctness edge of the fix (starvation recurs). IMPORTANT fits: "real maintainability or correctness issue, strongly prefer fixing before merge". I'll file it as IMPORTANT with concrete recommendations.

Very useful. Key observations:

1. **The `{branch}`-dispatch rules that the dead-head scenario hits**: `review-on-label` (limit 1, ref {branch}, notLabels: []), `rework-on-label` (limit 1, ref {branch}, notLabels: []), `review-on-issue-label`, `review-after-dev`, etc. NONE of them exclude `validation_failed`. So once a dead head is parked `validation_failed` by gh-922, `review-on-label`/`rework-on-label` still match it (if they carry agent:review/agent:rework) and keep attempting every tick, consuming fallthrough reserve each tick. With the reserve fixed at 3, FOUR simultaneously dead `{branch}` heads under one limit:1 rule re-starve the FIFO (4 candidates dead → slice(0,4) exhausted, no slot). Also interesting: `rework-on-validation-failed` (labels: ['validation_failed']) — a gh-922-parked PR MATCHES this rule! What does that rule do? It arms agent:rework on validation_failed PRs? Let me check: "rework-on-validation-failed limit=1 labels=['validation_failed'] notLabels=['agent:rework','ai_validating']" — this rule (per gh-757/gh-917 family) arms agent:rework on parked PRs... for MACHINE PRs (per the rework-on-red-gate description, guests keep the human-push semantics; machine PRs get a rework arm). If the gh-922 dead-head park stamps validation_failed on a MACHINE PR (ai-teammate's own PR with a deleted branch — rare but possible), rework-on-validation-failed would arm agent:rework → rework-on-label dispatches a rework leg on `{branch}` → dispatch fails no-ref again → MORE marker comments (from a second rule) → the count climbs faster; the park guard (`already parked`) prevents re-park, but each failed dispatch of rework-on-label ALSO writes markers... wait no — recordDispatchFailure returns early because labels contain validation_failed (item.labels fetched fresh from the query — the PR now carries validation_failed). So no marker spam. But an arm_rework localAction stamping agent:rework on a dead-head-parked machine PR is a wasted arm; rework-on-label will attempt + fail + yield every tick. Self-limiting, minor.

But the deeper interaction: does arm_rework's in-flight latch etc. care? Fine.

2. **`park-reset` rule** (labels: ['validation_failed'], limit 10) — the RESET ladder: probes human push newer than park → clears the label. The gh-922 park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` which keys the parkedSince/sha-change probes. Good — the gh-922 park integrates with the existing reset ladder. Note: `park-reset`'s probes were built for RED parks (checks semantics). For a dead-head park, the "human push newer" probe needs the branch to EXIST again — parkResetCommit walks the head chain of the CURRENT head... if the branch doesn't exist, uHead=null → fail closed → park stays. When the author restores/re-pushes the branch, the head exists again, and the actor check ("human push NEWER than the validation_failed event") — parkedSince reads the label-add timestamp (the park event) — the re-push is newer → clears. Correct integration.

3. **The tier void only matters for `priority_blocker` carriers.** OK.

4. **`review-on-label` notLabels is EMPTY** — so a parked PR keeps matching review-on-label forever until the park resets. Each tick: 1 failed dispatch + 1 early-return recordDispatchFailure (no comment spam — the parked guard works). The wasted-attempt-per-tick is by design ("re-matches until the ref is restored").

Now the >3-dead-heads starvation: to hit it you need 4+ dead-head candidates AHEAD of an alive candidate in one rule's tier-sorted list with limit such that limit+reserve < dead count. E.g. review-on-label limit:1 with 4 abandoned `agent:review` PRs. Possible but requires 4 abandoned labeled PRs. IMPORTANT vs SUGGESTION? The ticket's core complaint is starvation; the fix bounds it at 3 concurrent dead heads. I'll file IMPORTANT with concrete options (scale reserve with limit; or exclude validation_failed+dead-head from dispatch-rule queries via notLabels — accepting the semantic conflation; or bump reserve). Actually — hmm, let me reconsider. The engine loop breaks on `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit`, iterating up to len(tickets) = limit+3. If all limit+3 candidates fail, the tick ends with 0 processed. Next tick, same. So starvation persists beyond 3 dead heads. BUT the parked dead heads accumulate markers only up to the cap; after parking they're SILENT (no more comments). A 4th dead head would park too (3 ticks). So steady state: unlimited dead heads, all parked, all attempted every tick, all failing — starvation if dead count >= limit+reserve... wait no! Each dead head attempt = 1 API call that fails fast. The loop iterates ALL tickets (not just limit+3 — well, exactly limit+3 tickets). With 4+ dead heads and limit 1, the slice is 4 — all dead → alive candidates beyond position 4 never reached. Starved. Yes, the bound is real. IMPORTANT.

Hmm — although... realistically, do dead-head PRs accumulate? PR-as-carrier rules consume labels on dispatch (consumeLabels) — review-on-label: does it consume agent:review on dispatch? If consumeLabels removes agent:review when the leg dispatches successfully, a PR whose dispatch ALWAYS fails keeps agent:review (never consumed) and keeps matching forever. Yes — that's exactly the ticket scenario (pr-1615 kept priority_blocker and matched every tick).

So: 4+ abandoned PRs carrying agent:review (or agent:rework) with deleted branches = starvation returns. Plausible on busy repos over months. IMPORTANT.

5. **Another design check — `triggerFailMarks` reads ALL comments of the PR every failed tick** — one `github_get_pr_comments` call per failed dispatch per tick. Cheap enough.

6. **Now the item.labels check in recordDispatchFailure uses `item.labels`** — for the github PR source, item.labels = label names array. ✓ (tests pass with labels arrays).

7. **`String(expandedRef || '') !== String(item.branch)`**: for `review-on-issue-label` (ref '{branch}' but item issue-carrier with linked PR branch) — item.branch set? The issue path sets item.branch only when a linked OPEN PR exists. OK.

8. **DRY mode**: recordDispatchFailure returns early in DRY — no side effects in dry ticks. ✓ And the DRY dispatch in triggerWorkflow returns `undefined` (not true/false) — unchanged behavior.

9. **GraalJS compliance of new code**: `var` + plain functions everywhere; no arrow functions, no let/const, no template literals. `String.prototype.replace` with regex, `Object.assign`? Not used in new code except tests (tests run in GraalJS too — `Object.assign` used in tests: `Object.assign({ realSource: true }, ...)` — is Object.assign available in GraalJS? ES6 builtins — GraalJS supports ES2020+, yes. And existing tests already use Object.assign (I saw `Object.assign({}, RULE, ...)` in existing test code). Fine.

10. **triggerFailures.js requires nothing** — no require at all. Pack-require rule satisfied trivially. smAgent.js requires it hoisted at top (line ~150). ✓ gh-823 rule respected.

11. **`classifyTriggerError` false-positive surface**: `/\b422\b/.test(s) && /ref/i.test(s)` — a transient error message containing "422" and "ref" anywhere (e.g. "422: Unprocessable Entity — invalid input ... refresh_token") would classify no-ref → marker+park path on a non-dead head. Edge: a 422 about branch protection mentioning "required status checks... refs" — unlikely from a dispatch error. The classifier only drives COMMENT bookkeeping (worst case: spurious marker comments + park on a live head — that WOULD be bad: parking a live PR because its error text mentioned 422+ref... but the dispatch FAILED, so the PR isn't going anywhere this tick anyway; 3 such failures in a row = park. Eh — a persistently failing live head (e.g., workflow file 404 is classified transient ✓). Acceptable heuristic. Not a finding beyond maybe noting the message-shape coupling.

{"content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: the fixed 3-slot reserve bounds the starvation fix — 4+ dead heads re-starve the FIFO**

`TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE = 3` is a hard constant, and a parked (`validation_failed`) dead head **remains a dispatch candidate** — the dispatch rules that hit this failure mode (`review-on-label`, `rework-on-label`, `review-after-dev`, …) carry `notLabels: []`, so a parked PR keeps matching every tick and burns one failed dispatch (plus one reserve slot) per tick until the branch is restored.

Failure shape after this fix, for a `limit: 1` rule with **4+** simultaneously dead heads:

```text
candidates (tier-sorted, slice(0, limit + 3)) = [dead1, dead2, dead3, dead4]
→ dead1 fails (yield), dead2 fails (yield), dead3 fails (yield), dead4 fails (yield)
→ loop ends: 0 slot credits, the alive candidate at position 5 was never in the slice
→ FIFO starved again, every tick
```

Each dead head parks after 3 ticks and goes silent, but parked heads are never removed from candidacy, so abandoned `agent:review`/`agent:rework` PRs accumulate indefinitely on a busy repo — the bound is real, not theoretical.

Options, cheapest first:

1. Scale the reserve: `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE + parkedCount` or a simple `Math.max(3, …)` heuristic.
2. Bench dead-head-parked candidates at source level: `validation_failed` + head missing from the already-fetched `branchHeads` snapshot identifies a dead-head park without any comment scan (do **not** exclude all `validation_failed` — the `park-reset` rule must still find red-parked PRs).
3. Add `notLabels: ["validation_failed"]` to the `{branch}`-dispatch rules in `sm_github.json` — accepted cost: it conflates the red-park (gh-832) and dead-head-park semantics on the shared label.

At minimum, document the 3-dead-head bound next to the constant so the next starvation ticket doesn't start from zero.

Related dead end worth noting: a **machine-authored** PR with a deleted head gets parked, `rework-on-validation-failed` arms `agent:rework` on it, but the rework leg can never dispatch (dead branch) and no human push will ever clear the park — a permanent arm + a permanent failed attempt per tick. Consider exempting dead-head parks from the machine rework arm.

With the reserve fixed at 3, FOUR simultaneously dead `{branch}` heads under one limit:1 rule re-starve the FIFO (4 candidates dead → slice(0,4) exhausted, no slot). Also interesting: `rework-on-validation-failed` (labels: ['validation_failed']) — a gh-922-parked PR MATCHES this rule! What does that rule do? It arms agent:rework on validation_failed PRs? Let me check: "rework-on-validation-failed limit=1 labels=['validation_failed'] notLabels=['agent:rework','ai_validating']" — this rule (per gh-757/gh-917 family) arms agent:rework on parked PRs... for MACHINE PRs (per the rework-on-red-gate description, guests keep the human-push semantics; machine PRs get a rework arm). If the gh-922 dead-head park stamps validation_failed on a MACHINE PR (ai-teammate's own PR with a deleted branch — rare but possible), rework-on-validation-failed would arm agent:rework → rework-on-label dispatches a rework leg on `{branch}` → dispatch fails no-ref again → MORE marker comments (from a second rule) → the count climbs faster; the park guard (`already parked`) prevents re-park, but each failed dispatch of rework-on-label ALSO writes markers... wait no — recordDispatchFailure returns early because labels contain validation_failed (item.labels fetched fresh from the query — the PR now carries validation_failed). So no marker spam. But an arm_rework localAction stamping agent:rework on a dead-head-parked machine PR is a wasted arm; rework-on-label will attempt + fail + yield every tick. Self-limiting, minor.

But the deeper interaction: does arm_rework's in-flight latch etc. care? Fine.

2. **`park-reset` rule** (labels: ['validation_failed'], limit 10) — the RESET ladder: probes human push newer than park → clears the label. The gh-922 park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` which keys the parkedSince/sha-change probes. Good — the gh-922 park integrates with the existing reset ladder. Note: `park-reset`'s probes were built for RED parks (checks semantics). For a dead-head park, the "human push newer" probe needs the branch to EXIST again — parkResetCommit walks the head chain of the CURRENT head... if the branch doesn't exist, uHead=null → fail closed → park stays. When the author restores/re-pushes the branch, the head exists again, and the actor check ("human push NEWER than the validation_failed event") — parkedSince reads the label-add timestamp (the park event) — the re-push is newer → clears. Correct integration.

3. **The tier void only matters for `priority_blocker` carriers.** OK.

4. **`review-on-label` notLabels is EMPTY** — so a parked PR keeps matching review-on-label forever until the park resets. Each tick: 1 failed dispatch + 1 early-return recordDispatchFailure (no comment spam — the parked guard works). The wasted-attempt-per-tick is by design ("re-matches until the ref is restored").

Now the >3-dead-heads starvation: to hit it you need 4+ dead-head candidates AHEAD of an alive candidate in one rule's tier-sorted list with limit such that limit+reserve < dead count. E.g. review-on-label limit:1 with 4 abandoned `agent:review` PRs. Possible but requires 4 abandoned labeled PRs. IMPORTANT vs SUGGESTION? The ticket's core complaint is starvation; the fix bounds it at 3 concurrent dead heads. I'll file IMPORTANT with concrete options (scale reserve with limit; or exclude validation_failed+dead-head from dispatch-rule queries via notLabels — accepting the semantic conflation; or bump reserve). Actually — hmm, let me reconsider. The engine loop breaks on `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit`, iterating up to len(tickets) = limit+3. If all limit+3 candidates fail, the tick ends with 0 processed. Next tick, same. So starvation persists beyond 3 dead heads. BUT the parked dead heads accumulate markers only up to the cap; after parking they're SILENT (no more comments). A 4th dead head would park too (3 ticks). So steady state: unlimited dead heads, all parked, all attempted every tick, all failing — starvation if dead count >= limit+reserve... wait no! Each dead head attempt = 1 API call that fails fast. The loop iterates ALL tickets (not just limit+3 — well, exactly limit+3 tickets). With 4+ dead heads and limit 1, the slice is 4 — all dead → alive candidates beyond position 4 never reached. Starved. Yes, the bound is real. IMPORTANT.

Hmm — although... realistically, do dead-head PRs accumulate? PR-as-carrier rules consume labels on dispatch (consumeLabels) — review-on-label: does it consume agent:review on dispatch? If consumeLabels removes agent:review when the leg dispatches successfully, a PR whose dispatch ALWAYS fails keeps agent:review (never consumed) and keeps matching forever. {"content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: the fixed 3-slot reserve bounds the starvation fix — 4+ dead heads re-starve the FIFO**

`TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE = 3` is a hard constant, and a parked (`validation_failed`) dead head **remains a dispatch candidate** — the dispatch rules that hit this failure mode (`review-on-label`, `rework-on-label`, `review-after-dev`, …) carry `notLabels: []`, so a parked PR keeps matching every tick and burns one failed dispatch (plus one reserve slot) per tick until the branch is restored.

Failure shape after this fix, for a `limit: 1` rule with **4+** simultaneously dead heads:

```text
candidates (tier-sorted, slice(0, limit + 3)) = [dead1, dead2, dead3, dead4]
→ dead1 fails (yield), dead2 fails (yield), dead3 fails (yield), dead4 fails (yield)
→ loop ends: 0 slot credits, the alive candidate at position 5 was never in the slice
→ FIFO starved again, every tick
```

Each dead head parks after 3 ticks and goes silent, but parked heads are never removed from candidacy, so abandoned `agent:review`/`agent:rework` PRs accumulate indefinitely on a busy repo — the bound is real, not theoretical.

Options, cheapest first:

1. Scale the reserve: `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE + parkedCount` or a simple `Math.max(3, …)` heuristic.
2. Bench dead-head-parked candidates at source level: `validation_failed` + head missing from the already-fetched `branchHeads` snapshot identifies a dead-head park without any comment scan (do **not** exclude all `validation_failed` — the `park-reset` rule must still find red-parked PRs).
3. Add `notLabels: ["validation_failed"]` to the `{branch}`-dispatch rules in `sm_github.json` — accepted cost: it conflates the red-park (gh-832) and dead-head-park semantics on the shared label.

At minimum, document the 3-dead-head bound next to the constant so the next starvation ticket doesn't start from zero.

Related dead end worth noting: a **machine-authored** PR with a deleted head gets parked, `rework-on-validation-failed` arms `agent:rework` on it, but the rework leg can never dispatch (dead branch) and no human push will ever clear the park — a permanent arm + a permanent failed attempt per tick. Consider exempting dead-head parks from the machine rework arm.

...

```

`msg` is written verbatim into the comment body, and `triggerFailMarks` re-scans those bodies for `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/cap at <iso>` lines. An error message (or a crafted branch name flowing through one) containing an embedded newline plus a marker-shaped line could inflate its own head's attempt counter — e.g. jump straight to `attempt 3/3` and park on the first real failure.

Threat assessment: **low** — markers are keyed to the PR's own branch, the comments land on that same PR, and the worst case is an author accelerating the parking of their own dead PR (which a deleted branch achieves anyway). No cross-PR or privilege impact.

Cheap hardening: flatten the message before embedding — `msg.split('\n')[0]` (or `msg.replace(/\s+/g, ' ')`) — so a multi-line error can never carry a parseable marker line into the body.

1. **The `{branch}`-dispatch rules that the dead-head scenario hits**: `review-on-label` (limit 1, ref {branch}, notLabels: []), `rework-on-label` (limit 1, ref {branch}, notLabels: []), `review-on-issue-label`, `review-after-dev`, etc. NONE of them exclude `validation_failed`. So once a dead head is parked `validation_failed` by gh-922, `review-on-label`/`rework-on-label` still match it (if they carry agent:review/agent:rework) and keep attempting every tick, consuming fallthrough reserve each tick. With the reserve fixed at 3, FOUR simultaneously dead `{branch}` heads under one limit:1 rule re-starve the FIFO (4 candidates dead → slice(0,4) exhausted, no slot). Also interesting: `rework-on-validation-failed` (labels: ['validation_failed']) — a gh-922-parked PR MATCHES this rule! What does that rule do? It arms agent:rework on validation_failed PRs? Let me check: "rework-on-validation-failed limit=1 labels=['validation_failed'] notLabels=['agent:rework','ai_validating']" — this rule (per gh-757/gh-917 family) arms agent:rework on parked PRs... for MACHINE PRs (per the rework-on-red-gate description, guests keep the human-push semantics; machine PRs get a rework arm). ```text
candidates (tier-sorted, slice(0, limit + 3)) = [dead1, dead2, dead3, dead4]
→ dead1 fails (yield), dead2 fails (yield), dead3 fails (yield), dead4 fails (yield)
→ loop ends: 0 slot credits, the alive candidate at position 5 was never in the slice
→ FIFO starved again, every tick
```

Each dead head parks after 3 ticks and goes silent, but parked heads are never removed from candidacy, so abandoned `agent:review`/`agent:rework` PRs accumulate indefinitely on a busy repo — the bound is real, not theoretical.

Options, cheapest first:

1. Scale the reserve: `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE + parkedCount` or a simple `Math.max(3, …)` heuristic.
2. Bench dead-head-parked candidates at source level: `validation_failed` + head missing from the already-fetched `branchHeads` snapshot identifies a dead-head park without any comment scan (do **not** exclude all `validation_failed` — the `park-reset` rule must still find red-parked PRs).
3. Add `notLabels: ["validation_failed"]` to the `{branch}`-dispatch rules in `sm_github.json` — accepted cost: it conflates the red-park (gh-832) and dead-head-park semantics on the shared label.

At minimum, document the 3-dead-head bound next to the constant so the next starvation ticket doesn't start from zero.

Related dead end worth noting: a **machine-authored** PR with a deleted head gets parked, `rework-on-validation-failed` arms `agent:rework` on it, but the rework leg can never dispatch (dead branch) and no human push will ever clear the park — a permanent arm + a permanent failed attempt per tick. Consider exempting dead-head parks from the machine rework arm.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: raw `err.message` is interpolated into PR comments that a marker parser later scans**

```javascript
var msg = String((err && err.message) || err);
...
' The workflow dispatch failed with a non-retryable no-ref error (' + msg + ').' +
```

`msg` is written verbatim into the comment body, and `triggerFailMarks` re-scans those bodies for `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/cap at <iso>` lines. An error message (or a crafted branch name flowing through one) containing an embedded newline plus a marker-shaped line could inflate its own head's attempt counter — e.g. jump straight to `attempt 3/3` and park on the first real failure.

Threat assessment: **low** — markers are keyed to the PR's own branch, the comments land on that same PR, and the worst case is an author accelerating the parking of their own dead PR (which a deleted branch achieves anyway). No cross-PR or privilege impact.

Cheap hardening: flatten the message before embedding — `msg.split('\n')[0]` (or `msg.replace(/\s+/g, ' ')`) — so a multi-line error can never carry a parseable marker line into the body.

Actually the concerning case: can a malicious/odd branch name cause the regex to read a HIGHER count from the error message than intended? The error message is embedded in the comment body too: `'...no-ref error (' + msg + ').'`. msg = `422: No ref found for: <branch>`. That doesn't contain "trigger-failed". So no inflation via msg. 4. **TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE=3 magic number** — exported? It's a module-level var in githubSource.js but not exported (module.exports = { query, matchesGuards }). Tests use the literal behavior. Fine.

5. **The 3-dead-heads starvation bound** (analyzed earlier): with the reserve fixed at 3, a 4th simultaneously-dead head at limit:1 starves the FIFO again. Each dead head parks after 3 failures, so the steady-state number of dead heads in the candidate list equals the number of PRs whose authors abandoned dead branches (could exceed 3 on a busy repo). Parked heads stay candidates (the review-lane query doesn't exclude validation_failed). Residual starvation is real but bounded-scoped; the ticket asked for a bounded mitigation ("suggest 3"). I'll file an IMPORTANT? Hmm. Let me think about severity. The whole point of the ticket is to eliminate FIFO starvation. The fix eliminates it for up to 3 concurrent dead heads. Beyond that, starvation returns — though now each dead head is PARKED (labeled) and visible, and operators can bench them (the park comment tells the author to restore). Could the source simply EXCLUDE validation_failed items from candidate selection entirely? Then the number of dead heads in the list is bounded by the reserve + in-flight accumulation (3 failures ≈ 3 ticks per head — a new dead head takes 3 ticks to park, so at most a few non-parked dead heads exist at once). Excluding parked items at query time would make starvation essentially impossible: parked items never match, non-parked dead heads accumulate at 1 per 3 ticks and exit the pool when parked. Hmm — but would excluding them break other flows? The merge-window lanes use notLabels exclusions already. The review-on-label query does NOT exclude validation_failed today... Actually WAIT. Very useful. Key observations:

1. **The `{branch}`-dispatch rules that the dead-head scenario hits**: `review-on-label` (limit 1, ref {branch}, notLabels: []), `rework-on-label` (limit 1, ref {branch}, notLabels: []), `review-on-issue-label`, `review-after-dev`, etc. NONE of them exclude `validation_failed`. So once a dead head is parked `validation_failed` by gh-922, `review-on-label`/`rework-on-label` still match it (if they carry agent:review/agent:rework) and keep attempting every tick, consuming fallthrough reserve each tick. With the reserve fixed at 3, FOUR simultaneously dead `{branch}` heads under one limit:1 rule re-starve the FIFO (4 candidates dead → slice(0,4) exhausted, no slot). Also interesting: `rework-on-validation-failed` (labels: ['validation_failed']) — a gh-922-parked PR MATCHES this rule! What does that rule do? It arms agent:rework on validation_failed PRs? Let me check: "rework-on-validation-failed limit=1 labels=['validation_failed'] notLabels=['agent:rework','ai_validating']" — this rule (per gh-757/gh-917 family) arms agent:rework on parked PRs... for MACHINE PRs (per the rework-on-red-gate description, guests keep the human-push semantics; machine PRs get a rework arm). If the gh-922 dead-head park stamps validation_failed on a MACHINE PR (ai-teammate's own PR with a deleted branch — rare but possible), rework-on-validation-failed would arm agent:rework → rework-on-label dispatches a rework leg on `{branch}` → dispatch fails no-ref again → MORE marker comments (from a second rule) → the count climbs faster; the park guard (`already parked`) prevents re-park, but each failed dispatch of rework-on-label ALSO writes markers... wait no — recordDispatchFailure returns early because labels contain validation_failed (item.labels fetched fresh from the query — the PR now carries validation_failed). So no marker spam. But an arm_rework localAction stamping agent:rework on a dead-head-parked machine PR is a wasted arm; rework-on-label will attempt + fail + yield every tick. Self-limiting, minor.

But the deeper interaction: does arm_rework's in-flight latch etc. care? Fine.

2. **`park-reset` rule** (labels: ['validation_failed'], limit 10) — the RESET ladder: probes human push newer than park → clears the label. The gh-922 park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` which keys the parkedSince/sha-change probes. Good — the gh-922 park integrates with the existing reset ladder. Note: `park-reset`'s probes were built for RED parks (checks semantics). For a dead-head park, the "human push newer" probe needs the branch to EXIST again — parkResetCommit walks the head chain of the CURRENT head... if the branch doesn't exist, uHead=null → fail closed → park stays. When the author restores/re-pushes the branch, the head exists again, and the actor check ("human push NEWER than the validation_failed event") — parkedSince reads the label-add timestamp (the park event) — the re-push is newer → clears. Correct integration.

3. **The tier void only matters for `priority_blocker` carriers.** OK.

4. **`review-on-label` notLabels is EMPTY** — so a parked PR keeps matching review-on-label forever until the park resets. Each tick: 1 failed dispatch + 1 early-return recordDispatchFailure (no comment spam — the parked guard works). The wasted-attempt-per-tick is by design ("re-matches until the ref is restored").

Now the >3-dead-heads starvation: to hit it you need 4+ dead-head candidates AHEAD of an alive candidate in one rule's tier-sorted list with limit such that limit+reserve < dead count. E.g. review-on-label limit:1 with 4 abandoned `agent:review` PRs. Possible but requires 4 abandoned labeled PRs. IMPORTANT vs SUGGESTION? The ticket's core complaint is starvation; the fix bounds it at 3 concurrent dead heads. I'll file IMPORTANT with concrete options (scale reserve with limit; or exclude validation_failed+dead-head from dispatch-rule queries via notLabels — accepting the semantic conflation; or bump reserve). Actually — hmm, let me reconsider. The engine loop breaks on `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit`, iterating up to len(tickets) = limit+3. If all limit+3 candidates fail, the tick ends with 0 processed. Next tick, same. So starvation persists beyond 3 dead heads. BUT the parked dead heads accumulate markers only up to the cap; after parking they're SILENT (no more comments). A 4th dead head would park too (3 ticks). So steady state: unlimited dead heads, all parked, all attempted every tick, all failing — starvation if dead count >= limit+reserve... wait no! Each dead head attempt = 1 API call that fails fast. The loop iterates ALL tickets (not just limit+3 — well, exactly limit+3 tickets). With 4+ dead heads and limit 1, the slice is 4 — all dead → alive candidates beyond position 4 never reached. Starved. Yes, the bound is real. IMPORTANT.

Hmm — although... realistically, do dead-head PRs accumulate? PR-as-carrier rules consume labels on dispatch (consumeLabels) — review-on-label: does it consume agent:review on dispatch? If consumeLabels removes agent:review when the leg dispatches successfully, a PR whose dispatch ALWAYS fails keeps agent:review (never consumed) and keeps matching forever. Yes — that's exactly the ticket scenario (pr-1615 kept priority_blocker and matched every tick).

So: 4+ abandoned PRs carrying agent:review (or agent:rework) with deleted branches = starvation returns. Plausible on busy repos over months. IMPORTANT.

5. **Another design check — `triggerFailMarks` reads ALL comments of the PR every failed tick** — one `github_get_pr_comments` call per failed dispatch per tick. Cheap enough.

6. **Now the item.labels check in recordDispatchFailure uses `item.labels`** — for the github PR source, item.labels = label names array. ✓ (tests pass with labels arrays).

7. **`String(expandedRef || '') !== String(item.branch)`**: for `review-on-issue-label` (ref '{branch}' but item issue-carrier with linked PR branch) — item.branch set? The issue path sets item.branch only when a linked OPEN PR exists. OK.

8. **DRY mode**: recordDispatchFailure returns early in DRY — no side effects in dry ticks. ✓ And the DRY dispatch in triggerWorkflow returns `undefined` (not true/false) — unchanged behavior.

9. **GraalJS compliance of new code**: `var` + plain functions everywhere; no arrow functions, no let/const, no template literals. `String.prototype.replace` with regex, `Object.assign`? Not used in new code except tests (tests run in GraalJS too — `Object.assign` used in tests: `Object.assign({ realSource: true }, ...)` — is Object.assign available in GraalJS? ES6 builtins — GraalJS supports ES2020+, yes. And existing tests already use Object.assign (I saw `Object.assign({}, RULE, ...)` in existing test code). Fine.

10. **triggerFailures.js requires nothing** — no require at all. Pack-require rule satisfied trivially. smAgent.js requires it hoisted at top (line ~150). ✓ gh-823 rule respected.

11. **`classifyTriggerError` false-positive surface**: `/\b422\b/.test(s) && /ref/i.test(s)` — a transient error message containing "422" and "ref" anywhere (e.g. "422: Unprocessable Entity — invalid input ... refresh_token") would classify no-ref → marker+park path on a non-dead head. The second test even asserts `'422: Unprocessable Entity — invalid input'` → transient (no "ref" substring — wait, "invalid input" — does it contain "ref"? No. OK). Edge: a 422 about branch protection mentioning "required status checks... refs" — unlikely from a dispatch error. The classifier only drives COMMENT bookkeeping (worst case: spurious marker comments + park on a live head — that WOULD be bad: parking a live PR because its error text mentioned 422+ref... but the dispatch FAILED, so the PR isn't going anywhere this tick anyway; 3 such failures in a row = park. Eh — a persistently failing live head (e.g., workflow file 404 is classified transient ✓). Acceptable heuristic. Not a finding beyond maybe noting the message-shape coupling.

12. **The workflow budget**: failed candidates don't decrement `workflowBudget.remaining` ✓ (line 3735-3737: only on success). But `ensureWorkflowBudgetActiveCount` inside triggerWorkflow may still run…

The overfetch interacts with `validate-fresh` etc. — the engine's effectiveLimit for localAction rules: `budgetCapped = !rule.localTeammate && !rule.localAction` → for localAction rules effectiveLimit = rule.limit. The loop breaks at processedKeys >= effectiveLimit. Local actions push processedKeys on success only... wait — for localAction rules, e.g. `merge-validated` limit 1: the loop now iterates up to 4 candidates; a candidate whose merge FAILS (exception caught → console.error, no processedKeys push → continue) — the loop tries the NEXT candidate in the same tick. That's a behavior CHANGE for merge rules: pre-fix, limit:1 merge rules attempted exactly one PR per tick; now a failing merge (e.g. transient API error during merge) falls through to merging the NEXT PR in the same tick. Is that desired? For merge-validated, merging up to 4 PRs per tick when earlier ones fail — this actually accelerates the queue (similar spirit). But it also means up to 3 EXTRA merge attempts per tick on failures. Hmm, is there any rule where falling through could double-act? processedKeys guards idempotency per tick; each candidate's action is guarded by its own query labels (skipIfLabel etc.). The fallthrough only advances on FAILURE (no slot credit), so the successful dispatch count stays <= limit. For localActions, "failure" = exception → the action didn't complete → trying the next candidate is consistent with fail-open. Seems safe and arguably beneficial. But — subtle: `validate-armed` limit:1 — a candidate whose arm fails (exception) falls through to arming the NEXT PR in the same tick — fine.

BUT — one more: the loop `break`s on `workflowBudget.remaining <= 0` for dispatch rules; localAction rules ignore budget. OK.

**Findings:**

Parked heads stay candidates by design ("re-matches until restored") and each still burns one failed dispatch per tick per matching rule. Options: scale the reserve with limit, exclude parked candidates at source level, or add notLabels to the dispatch rules (accepting the red-park/dead-head-park label conflation). Suggest at least documenting the bound or following up.

2. **IMPORTANT — No test for the new validate_pr lane branch.** The repo rule: "All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing." The new try/catch + recordDispatchFailure + continue in the validate lane (smAgent.js:2707-2715) is untested — no test dispatches a failing CI in the validate lane and asserts marker/park/no-arm. The triggerWorkflow path is thoroughly tested; the validate path isn't.

3. **SUGGESTION — Same-tick double-record/park with multiple matching rules.** Two rules both dispatching on the same dead head in one tick (e.g. review-on-label + rework-on-validation-failed arm interplay) each record markers from their own stale `item.labels` snapshot → double marker comments, and a second rule can post a duplicate park comment in the same tick the first parks (park guard checks `item.labels` which lacks the just-added label). Self-limiting (next tick the label guard stops it), but a `tr` re-check or post-add label merge would make it airtight.

4. **SUGGESTION — Error-message marker-injection surface.** `recordDispatchFailure` interpolates the raw `err.message` into PR comments; the marker parser scans comment bodies. A crafted branch name / API error text containing a fake `⚠️ trigger-failed ... attempt 9/3` line could inflate its own head's count (self-park acceleration only — no privilege escalation, markers are keyed to the commenter's own PR/branch). Stripping newlines from `msg` (or excluding marker-shaped lines) would close it.

5. **SUGGESTION — Issue-carrier path has no fallthrough reserve** (`githubSource.js:524` `slice(0, limit)`): issue-carrier rules keep the pre-fix starvation shape for any persistent trigger failure (rarer — issue legs dispatch on `main`; only linked-PR-branch rules can hit no-ref). 6. **SUGGESTION — `classifyTriggerError` message-shape coupling.** `/\b422\b/ && /ref/i` — a transient error whose text contains "422" and "ref" (e.g. an unrelated "refresh" token mention) classifies head-dead and drives markers/park. The heuristic is documented and tested for the known shapes; a stronger signal would be the HTTP status code / structured error rather than message regex.

Actually — also check: does `rework-on-validation-failed`'s arm_rework respect the parked-head sha / gh-922 park? {"content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: the fixed 3-slot reserve bounds the starvation fix — 4+ dead heads re-starve the FIFO**

`TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE = 3` is a hard constant, and a parked (`validation_failed`) dead head **remains a dispatch candidate** — the dispatch rules that hit this failure mode (`review-on-label`, `rework-on-label`, `review-after-dev`, …) carry `notLabels: []`, so a parked PR keeps matching every tick and burns one failed dispatch (plus one reserve slot) per tick until the branch is restored.

Failure shape after this fix, for a `limit: 1` rule with **4+** simultaneously dead heads:

```text
candidates (tier-sorted, slice(0, limit + 3)) = [dead1, dead2, dead3, dead4]
→ dead1 fails (yield), dead2 fails (yield), dead3 fails (yield), dead4 fails (yield)
→ loop ends: 0 slot credits, the alive candidate at position 5 was never in the slice
→ FIFO starved again, every tick
```

Each dead head parks after 3 ticks and goes silent, but parked heads are never removed from candidacy, so abandoned `agent:review`/`agent:rework` PRs accumulate indefinitely on a busy repo — the bound is real, not theoretical.

Options, cheapest first:

1. Scale the reserve: `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE + parkedCount` or a simple `Math.max(3, …)` heuristic.
2. Bench dead-head-parked candidates at source level: `validation_failed` + head missing from the already-fetched `branchHeads` snapshot identifies a dead-head park without any comment scan (do **not** exclude all `validation_failed` — the `park-reset` rule must still find red-parked PRs).
3. Add `notLabels: ["validation_failed"]` to the `{branch}`-dispatch rules in `sm_github.json` — accepted cost: it conflates the red-park (gh-832) and dead-head-park semantics on the shared label.

At minimum, document the 3-dead-head bound next to the constant so the next starvation ticket doesn't start from zero.

Related dead end worth noting: a **machine-authored** PR with a deleted head gets parked, `rework-on-validation-failed` arms `agent:rework` on it, but the rework leg can never dispatch (dead branch) and no human push will ever clear the park — a permanent arm + a permanent failed attempt per tick. Consider exempting dead-head parks from the machine rework arm.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: raw `err.message` is interpolated into PR comments that a marker parser later scans**

```javascript
var msg = String((err && err.message) || err);
...
' The workflow dispatch failed with a non-retryable no-ref error (' + msg + ').' +
```

`msg` is written verbatim into the comment body, and `triggerFailMarks` re-scans those bodies for `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/cap at <iso>` lines. An error message (or a crafted branch name flowing through one) containing an embedded newline plus a marker-shaped line could inflate its own head's attempt counter — e.g. jump straight to `attempt 3/3` and park on the first real failure.

Threat assessment: **low** — markers are keyed to the PR's own branch, the comments land on that same PR, and the worst case is an author accelerating the parking of their own dead PR (which a deleted branch achieves anyway). No cross-PR or privilege impact.

Cheap hardening: flatten the message before embedding — `msg.split('\n')[0]` (or `msg.replace(/\s+/g, ' ')`) — so a multi-line error can never carry a parseable marker line into the body.

EXCLUDING validation_failed from review-on-label would change that semantics — parked-for-red PRs would never get review legs. That's a behavior change beyond this ticket. Hmm.

But for the DEAD-HEAD park specifically — the new gh-922 park reuses the SAME label `validation_failed`. So the label now carries two park semantics (red-park and dead-head-park) and any rule-level exclusion conflates them. The dead-head park comment text says "no legs are dispatched against it" — but the review lane will still attempt it. There's a genuine semantic-overload question here: reusing validation_failed for the dead-head park means the dead-head-parked PR is indistinguishable from a red-parked PR. An alternative would be a distinct label (e.g. `head_parked` / `dispatch_dead`) + tier void + exclusion from dispatch rules. So the label choice is per-ticket; NOT a finding against the PR. But each tick, the parked ones yield quickly (their dispatch fails fast ~1 API call each), and the alive candidate at position 4 still gets the slot if only 3 dead heads precede it. With the reserve fixed at 3, FOUR simultaneously dead `{branch}` heads under one limit:1 rule re-starve the FIFO (4 candidates dead → slice(0,4) exhausted, no slot). Also interesting: `rework-on-validation-failed` (labels: ['validation_failed']) — a gh-922-parked PR MATCHES this rule! What does that rule do? It arms agent:rework on validation_failed PRs? If the gh-922 dead-head park stamps validation_failed on a MACHINE PR (ai-teammate's own PR with a deleted branch — rare but possible), rework-on-validation-failed would arm agent:rework → rework-on-label dispatches a rework leg on `{branch}` → dispatch fails no-ref again → MORE marker comments (from a second rule) → the count climbs faster; the park guard (`already parked`) prevents re-park, but each failed dispatch of rework-on-label ALSO writes markers... wait no — recordDispatchFailure returns early because labels contain validation_failed (item.labels fetched fresh from the query — the PR now carries validation_failed). If consumeLabels removes agent:review when the leg dispatches successfully, a PR whose dispatch ALWAYS fails keeps agent:review (never consumed) and keeps matching forever. So: 4+ abandoned PRs carrying agent:review (or agent:rework) with deleted branches = starvation returns. Plausible on busy repos over months. IMPORTANT.

The overfetch interacts with `validate-fresh` etc. — the engine's effectiveLimit for localAction rules: `budgetCapped = !rule.localTeammate && !rule.localAction` → for localAction rules effectiveLimit = rule.limit. The loop breaks at processedKeys >= effectiveLimit. Is that desired? For merge-validated, merging up to 4 PRs per tick when earlier ones fail — this actually accelerates the queue (similar spirit). But it also means up to 3 EXTRA merge attempts per tick on failures. Hmm, is there any rule where falling through could double-act? processedKeys guards idempotency per tick; each candidate's action is guarded by its own query labels (skipIfLabel etc.). The fallthrough only advances on FAILURE (no slot credit), so the successful dispatch count stays <= limit. For localActions, "failure" = exception → the action didn't complete → trying the next candidate is consistent with fail-open. Seems safe and arguably beneficial. But — subtle: `validate-armed` limit:1 — a candidate whose arm fails (exception) falls through to arming the NEXT PR in the same tick — fine.

**Findings:**

1. **IMPORTANT — Fixed 3-slot fallthrough reserve bounds the starvation fix; parked dead heads remain dispatch candidates forever.** `TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE = 3` + non-exclusion of `validation_failed` from dispatch-rule queries (`review-on-label`/`rework-on-label` have `notLabels: []`): a 4th simultaneously-dead head under a limit:1 rule re-starves the FIFO (slice(0, limit+3) exhausted by dead candidates, each failing fast every tick). Parked heads stay candidates by design ("re-matches until restored") and each still burns one failed dispatch per tick per matching rule. Options: scale the reserve with limit, exclude parked candidates at source level, or add notLabels to the dispatch rules (accepting the red-park/dead-head-park label conflation). Suggest at least documenting the bound or following up.

2. **IMPORTANT — No test for the new validate_pr lane branch.** The repo rule: "All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing." The new try/catch + recordDispatchFailure + continue in the validate lane (smAgent.js:2707-2715) is untested — no test dispatches a failing CI in the validate lane and asserts marker/park/no-arm. The triggerWorkflow path is thoroughly tested; the validate path isn't.

3. **SUGGESTION — Same-tick double-record/park with multiple matching rules.** Two rules both dispatching on the same dead head in one tick (e.g. review-on-label + rework-on-validation-failed arm interplay) each record markers from their own stale `item.labels` snapshot → double marker comments, and a second rule can post a duplicate park comment in the same tick the first parks (park guard checks `item.labels` which lacks the just-added label). Self-limiting (next tick the label guard stops it), but a `tr` re-check or post-add label merge would make it airtight.

4. **SUGGESTION — Error-message marker-injection surface.** `recordDispatchFailure` interpolates the raw `err.message` into PR comments; the marker parser scans comment bodies. A crafted branch name / API error text containing a fake `⚠️ trigger-failed ... attempt 9/3` line could inflate its own head's count (self-park acceleration only — no privilege escalation, markers are keyed to the commenter's own PR/branch). Stripping newlines from `msg` (or excluding marker-shaped lines) would close it.

{"content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: the fixed 3-slot reserve bounds the starvation fix — 4+ dead heads re-starve the FIFO**

`TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE = 3` is a hard constant, and a parked (`validation_failed`) dead head **remains a dispatch candidate** — the dispatch rules that hit this failure mode (`review-on-label`, `rework-on-label`, `review-after-dev`, …) carry `notLabels: []`, so a parked PR keeps matching every tick and burns one failed dispatch (plus one reserve slot) per tick until the branch is restored.

Failure shape after this fix, for a `limit: 1` rule with **4+** simultaneously dead heads:

```text
candidates (tier-sorted, slice(0, limit + 3)) = [dead1, dead2, dead3, dead4]
→ dead1 fails (yield), dead2 fails (yield), dead3 fails (yield), dead4 fails (yield)
→ loop ends: 0 slot credits, the alive candidate at position 5 was never in the slice
→ FIFO starved again, every tick
```

Each dead head parks after 3 ticks and goes silent, but parked heads are never removed from candidacy, so abandoned `agent:review`/`agent:rework` PRs accumulate indefinitely on a busy repo — the bound is real, not theoretical.

Options, cheapest first:

1. Scale the reserve: `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE + parkedCount` or a simple `Math.max(3, …)` heuristic.
2. Bench dead-head-parked candidates at source level: `validation_failed` + head missing from the already-fetched `branchHeads` snapshot identifies a dead-head park without any comment scan (do **not** exclude all `validation_failed` — the `park-reset` rule must still find red-parked PRs).
3. Add `notLabels: ["validation_failed"]` to the `{branch}`-dispatch rules in `sm_github.json` — accepted cost: it conflates the red-park (gh-832) and dead-head-park semantics on the shared label.

At minimum, document the 3-dead-head bound next to the constant so the next starvation ticket doesn't start from zero.

Related dead end worth noting: a **machine-authored** PR with a deleted head gets parked, `rework-on-validation-failed` arms `agent:rework` on it, but the rework leg can never dispatch (dead branch) and no human push will ever clear the park — a permanent arm + a permanent failed attempt per tick. Consider exempting dead-head parks from the machine rework arm.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: same-tick multi-rule dispatch can double-record and post a duplicate park**

The already-parked guard reads the *query-time* label snapshot:

```javascript
if ((item.labels || []).indexOf('validation_failed') !== -1) return; // already parked
```

Within one tick, `item.labels` never refreshes. If two rules matching the same dead head both dispatch on `{branch}` in the same tick (realistic: `rework-on-validation-failed` arms `agent:rework` on parked machine PRs, putting the PR in `rework-on-label`'s lane alongside e.g. `review-on-issue-label`), the second rule's failed dispatch:

- posts a **second marker comment** from its own stale snapshot, inflating the per-tick count, and
- if it crosses the cap in the same tick the first rule parked, posts a **duplicate park comment** (the first rule's `addLabel` isn't visible to the second rule's guard).

Self-limiting — from the next tick the fresh query sees the label and every rule early-returns — so this is a comment-hygiene nit, not a correctness bug. If you want it airtight, re-read the label after `github_get_pr_comments` (one `github_get_issue`/PR read, or a tracker `getLabels`) before writing, or keep a per-tick `parkedThisTick` set on the module.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: raw `err.message` is interpolated into PR comments that a marker parser later scans**

```javascript
var msg = String((err && err.message) || err);
...
' The workflow dispatch failed with a non-retryable no-ref error (' + msg + ').' +
```

`msg` is written verbatim into the comment body, and `triggerFailMarks` re-scans those bodies for `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/cap at <iso>` lines. An error message (or a crafted branch name flowing through one) containing an embedded newline plus a marker-shaped line could inflate its own head's attempt counter — e.g. jump straight to `attempt 3/3` and park on the first real failure.

Threat assessment: **low** — markers are keyed to the PR's own branch, the comments land on that same PR, and the worst case is an author accelerating the parking of their own dead PR (which a deleted branch achieves anyway). No cross-PR or privilege impact.

Cheap hardening: flatten the message before embedding — `msg.split('\n')[0]` (or `msg.replace(/\s+/g, ' ')`) — so a multi-line error can never carry a parseable marker line into the body.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the `422` + `ref` message heuristic is shape-coupled**

```javascript
if (/\b422\b/.test(s) && /ref/i.test(s)) return 'no-ref';
```

Classification drives the durable record (marker comments + park), so a *transient* error whose text happens to contain both `422` and any `ref` substring ("refresh", "referer", a proxy body quoting "refs/…") would be treated as head-dead evidence and, after 3 ticks, park a live PR. The known GitHub shapes are covered by tests; the residual risk is third-party/proxy error text between the SM and the API.

The failure direction is bounded (the PR wasn't dispatchable that tick anyway, and `triggerFailParkCap=false` opts out), so this is polish, not a blocker. If you ever harden it: match the full GitHub shape (`/no ref found for: refs\//i`, case-insensitive) instead of the two-token heuristic, or classify from a structured status code when the SCM bridge exposes one.
